questions.stem: How do anticholinergics act at muscarinic receptors, and why can high acetylcholine levels overcome this?
questions.answer: They compete with ACh for the binding site; the block is competitive, so enough ACh overcomes it

questions.stem: Most anticholinergic drugs are non-selective and act much like ____.
Which anticholinergic subgroup blocks nicotinic receptors more than others?
Why do quaternary anticholinergics such as ipratropium cause few central effects?
questions.answer: They do not cross the blood-brain barrier or membranes readily

questions.stem: Anticholinergic syndrome mnemonic: 'Dry as a ____, mad as a hatter, hot as a hare, red as a beet, blind as a bat, full as a flask.'
Anticholinergic syndrome mnemonic: 'Dry as a bone, mad as a hatter, hot as a hare, red as a beet, blind as a ____, full as a flask.'
Anticholinergic syndrome is best compared with which toxicity caused by anticholinesterases?
Which anticholinergic is used as a cycloplegic?
Which anticholinergic is used for Parkinson's disease?
Which anticholinergic is used for overactive bladder?
What brand name is given for hyoscine butylbromide?
When ipratropium blocks presynaptic M2 receptors in the lung, what happens to acetylcholine release?
questions.answer: Extra ACh release, which may partly offset its M3 bronchoconstriction block

questions.stem: Which anticholinergic is relatively selective for M1 and M3 receptors?
In high doses, antimuscarinic drugs such as tricyclic antidepressants mimic ____ poisoning.
Why is an anticholinergic given with an anticholinesterase when reversing neuromuscular block?
questions.answer: To block the anticholinesterase's unwanted muscarinic effects

questions.stem: How should anticholinergic and anticholinesterase pairings be chosen when reversing neuromuscular block?
Which usual clinical atropine dose range often causes brief heart rate slowing?
Why do usual atropine doses cause brief slowing of the heart?
questions.answer: M1 block in the parasympathetic ganglion supplying the SA node

questions.stem: What modest heart rate change does atropine cause, in beats per minute?
Larger atropine doses cause progressive tachycardia by blocking which receptors on SA node cells?
By how many beats per minute does 2 mg IM atropine raise resting heart rate in young men?
Which three agonists stimulate parietal cells to secrete acid?
Muscarinic stimulation of which gastric cells releases histamine?
Why have atropine-type doses that cut gastric acid been replaced by H2 antagonists and PPIs?
questions.answer: They also affect saliva, accommodation, micturition and motility

questions.stem: How many days may accommodation and pupil reflexes take to recover after topical atropine?
Why are shorter-acting agents preferred as mydriatics over topical atropine?
questions.answer: Topical atropine lasts long, so accommodation and pupil reflexes recover slowly
